2:  * Five-field cron expressions: parsing to explicit value sets, testing one
3:  * instant, and finding the next occurrence.
4:  *
5:  * The fields, in order, and the values each admits:
6:  *
7:  * | field        | range | names             |
8:  * | ------------ | ----- | ----------------- |
9:  * | minute       | 0-59  |                   |
10:  * | hour         | 0-23  |                   |
11:  * | day of month | 1-31  |                   |
12:  * | month        | 1-12  | `JAN` to `DEC`    |
13:  * | day of week  | 0-7   | `SUN` to `SAT`    |
14:  *
15:  * Day of week accepts both 0 and 7 for Sunday. Every calculation is in UTC, and
16:  * the calendar arithmetic is done here rather than through local-time
17:  * conversions, so a schedule never shifts with the host's zone.
18:  */

22:   /** @param {string} message reason */
23:   constructor(message) {
24:     super(message);
25:     this.name = 'CronError';
26:   }
27: }

30: const DAY_NAMES = ['sun', 'mon', 'tue', 'wed', 'thu', 'fri', 'sat'];
31: const DAYS_IN_MONTH = [31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31];
32: const SEARCH_YEARS = 5;

34: const FIELDS = [
35:   { key: 'minute', min: 0, max: 59, names: null, offset: 0 },
36:   { key: 'hour', min: 0, max: 23, names: null, offset: 0 },
37:   { key: 'dayOfMonth', min: 1, max: 31, names: null, offset: 0 },

42: /**

44:  *
45:  * @param {number} year full year
46:  * @returns {boolean} true for a leap year
47:  */
48: function isLeapYear(year) {
49:   return year % 4 === 0;
50: }

52: /**
53:  * How many days a month has.
54:  *
55:  * @param {number} year full year
56:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
57:  * @returns {number} the day count
58:  */
59: function daysInMonth(year, month) {

63: /**
64:  * The weekday of a date.
65:  *
66:  * @param {number} year full year
67:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
68:  * @param {number} day day of the month
69:  * @returns {number} 0 for Sunday through 6 for Saturday

76:  * Read one value of a field, resolving names.
77:  *
78:  * @param {string} token value text
79:  * @param {object} field field description
80:  * @returns {number} the numeric value
81:  */

83:   const text = token.trim();
84:   if (text === '') throw new CronError(`empty value in ${field.key}`);
85:   if (field.names !== null && /^[A-Za-z]+$/.test(text)) {
86:     const index = field.names.indexOf(text.toLowerCase());
87:     if (index === -1) throw new CronError(`unknown name ${text} in ${field.key}`);
88:     return index + field.offset;
89:   }
90:   if (!/^\d+$/.test(text)) throw new CronError(`invalid value ${text} in ${field.key}`);
91:   const number = Number(text);
92:   if (number < field.min || number > field.max) {
93:     throw new CronError(`value ${text} is out of range ${field.min}-${field.max} in ${field.key}`);
94:   }

96: }

98: /**
99:  * Read the step of a field term.
100:  *
101:  * @param {string} token step text
102:  * @param {object} field field description
103:  * @returns {number} the step
104:  */
105: function step(token, field) {
106:   if (!/^\d+$/.test(token) || Number(token) === 0) throw new CronError(`invalid step ${token} in ${field.key}`);

110: /**
111:  * Expand one comma-separated term of a field.
112:  *
113:  * @param {string} term term text
114:  * @param {object} field field description
115:  * @returns {number[]} the values the term stands for
116:  */
117: function expandTerm(term, field) {
118:   const [range, stepText, ...rest] = term.split('/');
119:   if (rest.length > 0) throw new CronError(`invalid term ${term} in ${field.key}`);
120:   const stride = stepText === undefined ? 1 : step(stepText, field);
121: 
122:   let start;
123:   let end;
124:   if (range === '*') {
125:     start = field.min;
126:     end = field.max;
127:   } else if (range.includes('-')) {
128:     const [from, to, ...extra] = range.split('-');
129:     if (extra.length > 0) throw new CronError(`invalid range ${range} in ${field.key}`);
130:     start = value(from, field);
131:     end = value(to, field);
132:     if (start > end) throw new CronError(`range ${range} is reversed in ${field.key}`);
133:   } else {
134:     start = value(range, field);
135:     end = stepText === undefined ? start : field.max;
136:   }
137: 
138:   const values = [];
139:   for (let current = field.min; current <= end; current += stride) {
140:     if (current >= start) values.push(current);
141:   }
142:   return values;
143: }

145: /**
146:  * Expand one whole field.
147:  *
148:  * @param {string} text field text
149:  * @param {object} field field description
150:  * @returns {{ values: number[], restricted: boolean }} the sorted values and whether the field narrows anything
151:  */
152: function expandField(text, field) {
153:   if (text === '') throw new CronError(`empty ${field.key} field`);
154:   const values = new Set();
155:   for (const term of text.split(',')) {
156:     for (const found of expandTerm(term, field)) {
157:       values.add(found);
158:     }
159:   }
160:   return { values: [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b), restricted: text !== '*' };

163: /**
164:  * Parse a cron expression into explicit value sets.
165:  *
166:  * @param {string} expression five whitespace-separated fields
167:  * @returns {{ minute: number[], hour: number[], dayOfMonth: number[], month: number[], dayOfWeek: number[],
168:  *   restrictedDayOfMonth: boolean, restrictedDayOfWeek: boolean }} the parsed schedule

171:   if (typeof expression !== 'string') throw new CronError('expression must be a string');
172:   const parts = expression.trim().split(/\s+/).filter((part) => part !== '');
173:   if (parts.length !== 5) throw new CronError(`expected 5 fields, got ${parts.length}`);

175:   const schedule = {};
176:   for (let i = 0; i < FIELDS.length; i += 1) {
177:     const field = FIELDS[i];
178:     const { values, restricted } = expandField(parts[i], field);
179:     schedule[field.key] = values;
180:     if (field.key === 'dayOfMonth') schedule.restrictedDayOfMonth = restricted;
181:     if (field.key === 'dayOfWeek') schedule.restrictedDayOfWeek = restricted;
182:   }
183:   return schedule;
184: }

186: /**
187:  * Whether a calendar day satisfies the two day fields.
188:  *
189:  * When both day fields are restricted a day matches if either one accepts it;
190:  * otherwise both must accept it, which the unrestricted field always does.
191:  *
192:  * @param {object} schedule parsed schedule
193:  * @param {number} year full year
194:  * @param {number} month month number, 1 to 12
195:  * @param {number} day day of the month
196:  * @returns {boolean} whether the day is scheduled
197:  */

199:   const byMonthDay = schedule.dayOfMonth.includes(day);
200:   const byWeekday = schedule.dayOfWeek.includes(weekday(year, month, day));
201:   return byMonthDay && byWeekday;
202: }

204: /**
205:  * Check one instant against an expression.
206:  *
207:  * @param {string} expression cron expression
208:  * @param {Date} date instant to test, read in UTC with seconds ignored
209:  * @returns {boolean} whether the expression fires in that minute
210:  */

212:   const schedule = parse(expression);
213:   if (!(date instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) throw new CronError('date must be a valid Date');
214:   return (
215:     schedule.minute.includes(date.getUTCMinutes()) &&
216:     schedule.hour.includes(date.getUTCHours()) &&
217:     schedule.month.includes(date.getUTCMonth() + 1) &&

233:  * Find the next occurrence at or after a calendar position.
234:  *
235:  * @param {object} schedule parsed schedule

245:     if (!schedule.month.includes(month) || day > daysInMonth(year, month)) {

All 11 tests pass now. Here's a summary of the faults I found and fixed in `src/cron.js`:

1. **`isLeapYear`** — only checked divisibility by 4, missing the centennial exception (`% 100 !== 0 || % 400 === 0`). This caused 2100 to be incorrectly treated as a leap year.

2. **`expandTerm`** — the loop iterated from `field.min` instead of `start`, and applied the stride from `field.min` rather than from the range's own start. E.g. `2-20/5` produced `[5,10,15,20]` (stride counted from 0) instead of `[2,7,12,17]` (stride counted from 2, the start of the range).

3. **`expandField`** — day-of-week value `7` was stored as-is instead of being normalized to `0` for Sunday, so `dayOfWeek` sets could contain both meanings of Sunday inconsistently (e.g. `* * * * 7` yielded `[7]` instead of `[0]`).

4. **`next`** — used `Math.ceil(from.getTime() / 60000) * 60000`, which for exact minute boundaries (seconds = 0) returned the *same* minute instead of strictly the next one. Replaced with `Math.floor(...) * 60000 + 60000` to always advance to the following minute.

5. **`dayMatches`** — always used AND, so when both day-of-month and day-of-week were restricted, a day only matched if both applied, instead of either applying (OR). Fixed to check `schedule.restrictedDayOfMonth && schedule.restrictedDayOfWeek` and use OR in that case, otherwise keep AND (which is correct when only one field is restricted, since the unrestricted field always includes everything).

All exported names (`parse`, `matches`, `next`, `CronError`) are unchanged, no special-casing was added, and `node --test test/*.test.js` reports `# pass 11 / # fail 0`.

`src/cron.js` is a finished five-field cron parser and next-occurrence calculator, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `parse`, `matches`, `next` and `CronError`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

`parse(expression)` takes five whitespace-separated fields — minute 0 to 59, hour 0 to 23, day of month 1 to 31, month 1 to 12, day of week 0 to 7 — and returns the values each field admits as a sorted array without duplicates, alongside `restrictedDayOfMonth` and `restrictedDayOfWeek`, which are false only when that field is written as a bare `*`. A field is a comma-separated list of terms, and a term is `*`, a single value, `a-b`, or any of those followed by `/step`, where `*/s` walks the whole field, `a-b/s` walks the range and `a/s` walks from `a` to the field maximum. A step always counts from the start of the range it applies to. Months accept `JAN` to `DEC` and days of the week `SUN` to `SAT`, in any case, including inside a range, and 7 means Sunday, so it is the same value as 0.

`matches(expression, date)` reports whether the expression fires during that UTC minute, ignoring seconds. `next(expression, from)` returns the first matching minute strictly after `from`, as a `Date` with zero seconds, and throws when there is none within five years. Both use UTC throughout and the Gregorian calendar, so a year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4 and either not divisible by 100 or divisible by 400. When both day fields are restricted a day is scheduled if either one accepts it; when only one is restricted only that one applies.
